title: The Male Abstraction Bias in Internet Culture and Large Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2611.05730v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Two foundational aspects of human cognition, abstractness and gender, are typically examined as separable. Here, we find they are systematically linked throughout the entire space of concepts spanning single (N = 40,000) and multi-word expressions (N = 67,000): across billions of words and millions of images on the internet -- and across numerous measurement techniques -- more abstract concepts are more associated with men, an effect which replicates in languages around the world. This pattern not only holds across conceptual domains, but it also maps onto grammatical structure: verbs and adverbs are more abstract and more male-coded, a system-wide trace of stereotypes accentuating agentic qualities in men. Furthermore, this bias emerges in human and AI responses in free association tasks, indicating its internalization and its algorithmic reproduction. translated_title: 互联网文化与大型语言模型中的男性抽象偏差
translated_abstract: 抽象性和性别是人类认知的两个基础维度，通常被作为相互独立的变量来研究。本研究发现，它们在覆盖单词表达（N = 40,000）和多词表达（N = 67,000）的整个概念空间中系统性关联：在互联网上数十亿词汇和数百万图像中——并经过多种测量技术的验证——越抽象的概念越与男性相关联，这一效应在世界各地的语言中均可复现。该模式不仅在各个概念领域普遍成立，还映射到语法结构上：动词和副词更抽象且更带有男性色彩，这是强调男性主动性特质的刻板印象在系统层面的痕迹。此外，这种偏差还出现在人类和AI在自由联想任务中的反应里，表明其已被人类内化并被算法复制。男性抽象偏差可能是多种刻板印象的共同基础，并将其统一起来……
tldr: 研究发现互联网文化和大型语言模型中存在系统性的“男性抽象偏差”——越抽象的概念越与男性相关联，该偏差跨越不同语言、概念领域和语法结构（动词、副词更抽象且更男性化），并被人类内化和AI算法复制。
en_tdlr: This study reveals a systematic "male abstraction bias" in internet culture and large language models, where more abstract concepts are more strongly associated with men—a pattern spanning languages, conceptual domains, and grammatical structure (verbs and adverbs are more abstract and male-coded), internalized by humans and reproduced by AI algorithms.
